_about: ONE source of truth for each WordPress.org Polyglots team's style rules (owner rulings 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-04). Read by engine/engine/i18n/style_rules.py and, as a BYTE-IDENTICAL copy, by Tranzly (wp/plugins/tranzly/includes/core/data/style-rules.json -> includes/core/class-style-rules.php). Edit HERE, then: cp engine/engine/i18n/style_rules.json wp/plugins/tranzly/includes/core/data/style-rules.json. Both implementations must pass style_rules_fixtures.json (pytest + PHPUnit). 'prompt' is the register/conventions guidance given to AI translation models, read from the team's own guide on 'accessed'.

fr.prompt: Use formal, simple French: address the reader as "vous", never "tu". Short clear sentences, avoid the passive, keep the source tone, never translate literally. Use the infinitive for button actions ("Enregistrer") and the imperative for help text. Capitalise only sentence starts, proper nouns and acronyms (also in titles). Use inclusive wording: neutral phrasing first, then doublets, the median dot only when space is tight. Keep theme/plugin names and URLs.
fr.prompt_quote: Privilégiez un langage formel. Le « vous » plutôt que le « tu ».

de.prompt: Address the reader informally with lower-case "du" (a separate formal "Sie" branch exists). Write active, short sentences understandable to non-technical users; avoid colloquialisms, dialect and buzzwords. Keep imperatives as imperatives, but UI commands use the infinitive ("Benutzer hinzufügen"); titles use nominalised verbs ("Hinzufügen von Benutzern"), "How to" becomes "So …". Do not translate plugin/theme names; use metric units and 24-hour time.
de.prompt_quote: Bei der Übersetzung von WordPress verwenden wir als Standard die informelle Schreibweise (kleingeschriebenes „du“).

es.prompt: Use informal Spanish, addressing the reader as "tú" rather than "usted". Translate contextually, not literally, and prefer genuine Spanish words for concepts and actions. Capitalise only the first word of UI element names ("Subir archivo", never "Subir Archivo"). Do not translate theme or plugin names. Use "sitio" for "site"/"blog" references per the guide.
es.prompt_quote: Usamos español informal, se prefiere el «tú» al «usted».

ru.prompt: Address the user with polite lower-case "вы" (never "ты", never capitalised "Вы"). Leave names of internet services and products untranslated and undeclined ("имя пользователя Facebook"). Use the letter "ё". Avoid slang and do not add emoji absent from the source. Avoid needless repetition and filler such as "вы должны" / "вы можете". Follow standard (Microsoft-style) terminology where the glossary is silent.
ru.prompt_quote: К пользователю принято обращаться на «вы» (не на «ты» и не на «Вы»).

pl.prompt: Address the user directly in the second person singular, as the guide's set phrases do ("nie posiadasz uprawnienia", "Zamierzasz…"); write personal pronouns in lower case. Decline "WordPress" normally (WordPressa, WordPressie). Use the team's terms: "wtyczka" for plugin, "motyw" for theme, "witryna" for site, "kokpit" for dashboard, "włącz" rather than "aktywuj" except for accounts/sites.
pl.prompt_quote: zaimki osobowe — piszemy wielką literą tylko w korespondencji, w tłumaczeniu zawsze z małej; „Sorry, you are not allowed to…” → „Przepraszamy, nie posiadasz uprawnienia do…”

ro.prompt: Use the informal style, second person singular, keeping the source tone; avoid gendered references ("Are you sure?" → "Sigur?"). Buttons and single actions use the 2nd-person-singular imperative ("Salvează", "Adaugă titlu"); when the app reports its own action use 1st person singular ("Am actualizat articolul."). No capitals inside sentences except names of commands, pages, buttons, themes or proper nouns. Dates d.m.Y, 24-hour time; keep plugin/theme names.
ro.prompt_quote: Tradu folosind stilul informal, la persoana a II-a singular, respectând tonul, colocvialitatea.

el.prompt: Address the reader in the plural: translate "you" as "εσείς", never "εσύ". Keep the translation easy for non-technical users, with short clear sentences; avoid the passive and long sentences; reflect the source tone; do not translate literally. Use the infinitive/verbal-noun form for buttons ("Αποθήκευση αλλαγών") and the imperative for help text ("Σύρετε…"). Capitalise only the start of a sentence. Do not translate theme or plugin names.
el.prompt_quote: Χρησιμοποιήστε πληθυντικό. Το “you” μεταφράζεται σε «εσείς» και όχι σε «εσύ».

cs.prompt: Translation should be formal and free of slang; avoid literal translation and English word order. Usually omit "you"/"your" rather than translating them. Drop "Sorry" and similar apologies ("Nemáte dostatečné oprávnění"). WordPress is not a person: use nouns, not first person ("Instalace", not "Instaluji"). Capitalise only the first word. Do not translate plugin/theme names, but decline them and WordPress normally.
cs.prompt_quote: Nepoužívejte slang, překlad by měl být formální.

sr.prompt: Translate only in Cyrillic script. Address the user in the second person plural with a lower-case "в" in possessives ("Ваш" is written "ваш"); never use the second person singular. Labels that directly perform an action (buttons, links) use the second-person-singular imperative ("Додај", "Обриши"). Capitalise only the first word of a sentence. Put the day before the month and prefer month names; convert to 24-hour time.
sr.prompt_quote: Подразумевани начин обраћања је у другом лицу множине. Овде је важно водити рачуна да се користи мало в у присвојним заменицима.

bg.prompt: Address the user in the second person plural, writing polite pronouns in lower case ("вас", not "Вас"). For UI commands use nouns rather than the imperative ("Преглед", "Добавяне"). Seek natural Bulgarian, not word-for-word; prefer a definite noun over "this" + noun; drop "Sorry" at the start of errors; avoid the calque "можете да" in favour of direct constructions. Do not capitalise every word of headings.
bg.prompt_quote: Използвайте второ лице, множествено число, там където на английски има второ лице.

nl.prompt: This is the default (non-formal) nl_NL style: friendly, simple, active, concise Dutch close to the source; do not use "alstublieft"/"a.u.b." (the separate formal variant uses "u"/"uw"). Drop jovial greetings and jokes ("Howdy", "Sorry"). Keep theme/plugin/brand names, links and common technical terms (e.g. "Update"). Capitalise only the first word of titles. Keep verbs in a consistent position. Use Dutch date formats and 24-hour time.
nl.prompt_quote: Formeel wijkt in zoverre af van de standaard, dat we daarin “u” en “uw” gebruiken als vertaling voor “you” en “your”. In standaard gebruiken we geen “alstublieft” en “a.u.b.”

vi.prompt: The guide states no explicit register; its examples address the reader as "bạn" ("Tài khoản của bạn"). Do not translate proper nouns or brand/theme names (WordPress, Twenty Sixteen). Do not carry English mid-phrase capitals over ("Chỉnh sửa hồ sơ của tôi"). Write numbers as words when the source does. Use Vietnamese date order with day before month and 24-hour time.
vi.prompt_quote: Nếu bạn thêm một video… / Tài khoản của bạn đã được kích hoạt!

te.prompt: Write user-to-computer commands in the singular ("తొలగించు") and the machine's instructions and questions to the user in the honorific form ("సైటుని చూడండి"). Use natural Telugu word order and modern forms, preferring native Telugu words in current use. If no Telugu word exists, transliterate the English word and end it in -u so it inflects naturally ("ఫైలు", plural "ఫైళ్ళు"). Keep the source's punctuation marks.
te.prompt_quote: కంప్యూటరు/మెషిన్ వాడుకరికి ఇచ్చే సూచనలూ, అడిగే ప్రశ్నలనూ గౌరవవచనంలో వ్రాయాలి.

ar.prompt: Write contemporary Modern Standard Arabic, never dialect. Convey meaning rather than word-for-word. Keep brand, organisation and company names in the original language unless a standard Arabic form exists. Use inclusive wording where possible and make gender explicit only when the source means one gender. Render commands as Arabic verbal nouns ("فتح ملف") unless the imperative is clearly needed. Use Western digits (1, 2, 3) and the common Gregorian month names (يناير…).
ar.prompt_quote: استخدام لغة عربية فصحى ومعاصرة، بدلاً من اللهجة المحلية.

ja.prompt: Write friendly, clear, concise, active Japanese that non-technical users understand; convey meaning, not literal wording. Omit "あなた/あなたの" when unnatural (use お使いの / 自分の or drop it). Avoid the passive. Drop a leading "Sorry" in errors. Headings: noun ending or plain form; list items: plain する form; buttons: drop the します ending. Wrap menu items/button labels in 「」. Never translate or transliterate WordPress or theme/plugin names.
ja.prompt_quote: 英語で “You” や “Your” とあっても、日本語にしたときに不自然な場合は「あなた」「あなたの」を入れない

is.note: No published is_IS style guide; register MEASURED from the team's own wp/dev translations (2026-10-05: 254 þú-paradigm forms, 0 formal þér/yður/yðar over 8,262 msgstr) and ruled for our own surfaces by the owner on 2026-10-05 ("use þú").
is.prompt: Address the reader informally as "þú" throughout (þig, þér as dative, þín, þinn/þín/þitt); never the formal "þér" as a subject or "yður"/"yðar". Verbs agree with þú ("þú getur", never "þér getið") and instructions use the singular imperative ("Smelltu", "Veldu", "Sláðu inn", never "Smellið"/"Veljið"). Write clear, short, natural modern Icelandic, not word-for-word; prefer established Icelandic computing terms over English loanwords. Do not translate plugin/theme names.

it.prompt: Use the informal "tu" (second person singular verbs, never third person, plural or infinitive), with a tone slightly more formal than speech. Easy, short, active sentences; reflect the source tone; never translate literally or idioms word for word. Do not humanise software; never translate a leading "Please". Keep technical terms with no Italian equivalent. No Title Case; lower-case days/months; English words stay invariant in the plural ("dei plugin").
it.prompt_quote: Esprimi i verbi nella seconda persona singolare (non in terza persona, non al plurale o all’infinito), in pratica usa il “tu”.

pt.prompt: Match WordPress's informal, polite tone in Brazilian Portuguese, using "você" and simple words ("Use", not "Utilize"); translate organically, not literally; drop "please" and "successfully". Avoid gendered forms by rephrasing ("Agradecemos a ajuda"). Buttons and action links use the infinitive ("Atualizar"). Capitalise only the first word and proper nouns; months/languages lower case. Keep brand, plugin and theme names. Dates d/m/Y, 24-hour time.
pt.prompt_quote: as mensagens do WordPress (principalmente mensagens informativas) tendem a ter um tom informal e educado em inglês. Procure realizar o equivalente no português

hr.prompt: Use the formal form of address: the computer addresses the user in the second person plural, out of respect but without capitalising "v"; user commands to the computer are in the first person singular imperative ("Obriši smeće"); results are impersonal ("Brisanje nije moguće", never "Ne mogu obrisati"). Omit "your" unless needed, using "svoj" where it applies. Use "je li"/inversion instead of "da li". Do not translate plugin/theme names. 24-hour time.
hr.prompt_quote: Računalo nije živo biće, pa kada računalo komunicira s korisnikom, obraća mu se u drugom licu množine – točnije, iz poštovanja, ali bez kapitaliziranja slova ‘v’.

id.prompt: Translate "you" as "Anda" for a general audience ("Saudara" for unknown readers); never address readers by first name. Keep the tone friendly, short and clear but professional; use "Silakan" for "Please" and "Jangan" for "Do not". Capture meaning, not word for word, and localise jokes. Follow PUEBI grammar. Keep WordPress and trademarked product names unchanged. Dates as "7 Januari 2008", 24-hour time, dot for thousands and comma for decimals.
id.prompt_quote: Untuk menerjemahkan “you”, gunakan “Anda” (untuk audiens umum) atau “Saudara” (untuk audiens yang tidak diketahui atau memiliki posisi/jabatan yang lebih rendah).

sk.prompt: Use formal Slovak: address the user with "vy" (vykanie), never "ty", and write vy/vám with a lower-case v. Translate organically, not literally, and without slang. Write month and day names in lower case; dates as "1. január 2013" or "5. 7. 2013", time "15:01". Translate "#" meaning a number as "č." and "&" as "a".
sk.prompt_quote: Slovenský preklad WordPress je formálny. V preklade používateľovi netykáme, používame vykanie. Slovo vy, vám a pod. píšeme s malým písmenom v.

pt_PT.prompt: Use formal European Portuguese, wherever possible the impersonal infinitive (no specific person), and remove gender references for inclusiveness. Use the spelling from before the 1990 Orthographic Agreement (pre-AO90). Translate as many terms as possible into Portuguese, contextually rather than literally, but keep jargon such as "plugin" and "widget". Capitalise only the first word of system elements. Use -mente adverbs sparingly; acronyms take no plural.
pt_PT.prompt_quote: Na tradução oficial usa-se o português formal, sempre que possível no infinitivo impessoal

da.prompt: Address the reader as "du" ("I"/"de" only when clearly speaking to several people). Write easy, friendly, short, active modern everyday Danish that reads as native, not word-for-word; follow the source's style. Skip jokes that do not work naturally in Danish. Avoid slang and narrow jargon. Capitalise only the first word of headings; brand names follow the original. Do not translate plugin/theme names. No full stop after headings or button labels.
da.prompt_quote: I sprogversionen da_DK bruger vi generelt tiltaleformen ”du”.

sv.prompt: Address the reader as "du" throughout ("ni" only when obviously speaking to several people). Write easy, friendly, short, active modern everyday Swedish that reads as native, not word-for-word. Skip jokes that do not work naturally. Avoid slang and narrow jargon. Use lower case in headings beyond the first word; brand names follow the original. Do not translate plugin/theme names. No full stop after headings or button text; write "procent" in running text.
sv.prompt_quote: I språkversionen sv_SE använder vi genomgående tilltalsformen ”du”.

ca.prompt: Use a more formal tone than English. When the software addresses the user, use the second person plural "vós" form, singular agreement ("esteu segur"), and avoid writing the pronoun "vós" explicitly. Commands the user gives the computer (menus, options) use the 2nd-person-singular imperative ("Edita", "Obre"), never the infinitive. Do not humanise the computer (no "Sorry"). Translate gerund titles as noun phrases or infinitives.
ca.prompt_quote: Quan l’ordinador es dirigeix a l’usuari (tant en quadres de diàleg com en documentació), en anglès es fa servir sempre la forma «you», del tot neutra en termes de formalitat. En català, en canvi, es fa servir la forma «vós».

zh.prompt: Translate to the standard of 信·达·雅: faithful, fluent, apt. Plugin, theme and author names may be translated only if it reads naturally and keeps the meaning, with the original name in parentheses at first mention ("查询监视器（Query Monitor）"); otherwise keep the original. Follow the glossary for fixed terms. Do not copy-convert Traditional Chinese translations. Keep correct brand casing (GitHub). Use full-width Chinese punctuation.
zh.prompt_quote: 「信」指意义不悖原文，即是译文要准确，不偏离，不遗漏，也不要随意增减意思

zh_TW.prompt: Write in Taiwan Traditional Chinese with Taiwanese IT vocabulary (no other Chinese variants, fads or retired terms). Make overly casual source text more rigorous, and avoid superlatives. Do not translate company, product, service, plugin, theme, plan, API names or foreign personal names. Avoid the passive ("已刪除這個檔案"). Mark clickable UI strings as [控制台]. Embedded English words: singular, first letter capitalised. Use Arabic numerals.
zh_TW.prompt_quote: 請在翻譯成台灣中文內容時加以轉換，改為較為嚴謹的方式展示譯文。

prompt_skipped.he: Guide fetched (https://he.wordpress.org/translate-wordpress/) but it states no register or conventions beyond 'do not translate word for word, write for Hebrew readers in Israel'; it links only to the global handbook and glossary.
